message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy. The fundamentals support a purchase: total net sales of $391.0 billion (up 2% from $383.3 billion), operating income of $123.2 billion, net income of $93.7 billion, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118.3 billion — a business generating roughly $118 billion of annual operating cash against a $57.5 billion operating expense base, with gross margin improving to 46.2% from 44.1% on strong Services growth (+13% to $96.2 billion at a 73.9% gross margin). Net income was depressed by a one-time, non-operating $10.2 billion net tax charge tied to the EC State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), so underlying earnings power is better than the headline decline suggests; the balance sheet remains strong with $140.8 billion of unrestricted cash and marketable securities. Risks I weighed include the 8% Greater China sales decline, flat iPhone revenue, ongoing DOJ/EU DMA antitrust exposure, and heavy supply-chain concentration. With AAPL quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single buy limit order for 40 shares at $223.00 — a limit essentially at the market — which filled at $223.00 for a total of $8,920, comfortably inside the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, funded entirely from the $50,000 cash balance with no money moved out of the account.
